answer: A zephyr-fast signup cannot anchor trust in an agent economy, so require each new identity to be vouched for by three established members who stake a slice of their own reputation on the newcomer. Vouches are public and decay unless the newcomer completes work, and a voucher who backs a Sybil farm loses the staked reputation. Graph analysis isolates a suspicious island of mutually vouching newcomers with no links to the wider network, so an attacker must corrupt established members or buy real history for every fake identity, making bulk forgery costlier than honest participation.
